title: Famous Firms, Earnings Clusters, and the Stock Market
one_line: E-mini S&P futures rose ~0.34% in the 24 hours before the most prominent after-close earnings clusters of famous firms (vs 0.02% on a typical day; Sharpe ~4.5, 1999-2018); holding only ~12 such days a year captured nearly two-thirds of the annual excess return.

findings.statement: Market +0.34% in the 24h before prominent PM (after-close) earnings clusters vs +0.02% typical; normal volatility; annualized Sharpe ~4.5.
findings.evidence: E-mini minute data 1999-2018; 3 most prominent PM clusters in each of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct, ranked by prior-year Dow Jones news count.

findings.statement: ~0.11% the evening before, ~0.23% during the pre-announcement trading day.
Only after-close clusters; pre-open clusters show no effect.
No correlation between pre- and post-announcement returns (not leakage).
~12 days a year ≈ two-thirds of the annual excess return.

why.pattern: Attention + short-sale constraints: differences of opinion before high-attention news push prices up.

reported_results.headline: E-mini S&P futures rose ~0.34% in the 24 hours before the most prominent after-close earnings clusters of famous firms (vs 0.02% on a typical day; Sharpe ~4.5, 1999-2018); holding only ~12 such days a year captured nearly two-thirds of the annual excess return.

tradable_edge: Long ES for the 24 hours before the three most-watched after-close mega-cap earnings clusters each earnings month — see spec famous_earnings_cluster_es.
angles: Long ES 16:00 two days before → 16:00 on the announcement day for top PM clusters
data_fit: ES 1-min covers it; needs a mega-cap earnings calendar (public).
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 3), not by the weekly pipeline.
